writtenTo: Young people and all who seek wisdom
importantNotes: 'The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge' (1:7) — the book's foundational principle.
Proverbs are general principles, not absolute promises — they describe how life usually works.
Lady Wisdom vs. Lady Folly (chs. 1-9) personify the two paths available to every person.
The Proverbs 31 woman describes the ideal of wisdom applied to daily life.
Solomon wrote 3,000 proverbs (1 Kings 4:32); Proverbs contains a curated selection.

chapters.1: The purpose of Proverbs — to gain wisdom; Lady Wisdom's warning against ignoring her.
chapters.2: Seek wisdom like hidden treasure — it protects from evil and wrong paths.
chapters.3: Trust in the LORD with all your heart; wisdom brings blessing and security.
chapters.4: A father's instruction — get wisdom above all else; guard your heart.
chapters.5: Warning against adultery — drink water from your own cistern.
chapters.6: Warnings against laziness, dishonesty, and the seven things God hates.
chapters.7: A vivid warning against the seduction of the adulterous woman.
chapters.8: Wisdom's speech — she was with God at creation; those who find her find life.
chapters.9: The two invitations — Lady Wisdom's feast vs. Lady Folly's trap.
chapters.10: Proverbs of Solomon: contrasts between the wise and the foolish, righteous and wicked.
chapters.11: Proverbs on integrity, generosity, and the consequences of righteousness vs. wickedness.
chapters.12: Proverbs on discipline, hard work, truthful speech, and wise living.
chapters.13: Proverbs on guarding your words, the value of discipline, and walking with the wise.
chapters.14: Proverbs on wisdom in the home, fearing the LORD, and caring for the poor.
chapters.15: Proverbs on gentle speech, the eyes of the LORD, and the joy of wisdom.
chapters.16: Proverbs on God's sovereignty over plans, pride before a fall, and gracious speech.
chapters.17: Proverbs on friendship, the tongue, family conflict, and a cheerful heart as medicine.
chapters.18: Proverbs on the power of words, the name of the LORD as a strong tower, and listening.
chapters.19: Proverbs on patience, kindness to the poor, discipline, and the fear of the LORD.
chapters.20: Proverbs on wine, laziness, honesty in business, and waiting on the LORD.
chapters.21: The king's heart is in God's hands; proverbs on justice, listening, and planning.
chapters.22: A good name is better than riches; train up a child in the way he should go.
chapters.23: Sayings of the wise — warnings about gluttony, wealth-chasing, and alcohol.
chapters.24: More sayings of the wise — do not envy the wicked; wisdom builds the house.
chapters.25: More proverbs of Solomon collected by Hezekiah's men — humility, patience, speech.
chapters.26: Proverbs about fools, sluggards, gossips, and the dangers of deception.
chapters.27: Proverbs on friendship, accountability, diligence, and the value of honest rebuke.
chapters.28: Proverbs on justice, integrity, confession of sin, and the danger of greed.
chapters.29: Proverbs on discipline, vision, humility, and the contrast between righteous and wicked rule.
chapters.30: The sayings of Agur — humility before God; numerical proverbs about amazing things.
chapters.31: The sayings of King Lemuel; the poem of the virtuous woman (Proverbs 31 wife).
